thread:
jess-support: customer filed a support ticket: tool call failing when message contains certain emoji family sequences. customer request_id: req_8a3f2c9
jess-support: pasted the cURL they used:
```bash
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/call \\
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx\" \\
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \\
  -d '{\n    \"tool\": \"create-note\",\n    \"args\": \"{\\\"title\\\":\\\"Sync\\\",\\\"body\\\":\\\"Agenda: sync + emojis \ud83d\udc68\u200d\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udc67\u200d\ud83d\udc66\\\"}\"}'
```

oliver-eng: quick read — looks like they double-serialized args (args is a JSON string). that makes unicode escaping fragile. do we have server logs?

jess-support: sanitized log snippet from our parser:
```
2024-06-17T15:12:03Z ERROR toolcall: parse args failed req=req_8a3f2c9 error=\"json: invalid UTF-8 in string literal\"\nstack: runtime/json.(*Decoder).decodeString +0x2c
```

lisa-ml: reproduced locally with identical payload. inner string contains a ZWJ family sequence. the bytes look like valid UTF-8 when read raw, but because the client double-encoded and used a non-utf8-preserving escape path we hit a lone-surrogate/invalid sequence during our inner-unmarshal.

oliver-eng: does this fail for all emoji or only chained ZWJ ones? customer said single emoji like thumbs-up works. they sent family using chain: \ud83d\udc68\u200d\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udc67\u200d\ud83d\udc66 (ZWJ chain).

jess-support: confirmed thumbs-up \ud83d\udc4d succeeded. only ZWJ family fails.

lisa-ml: root causes we see: (1) clients sending args as a serialized JSON string (double-encoding) so inner escaping matters; (2) some client libraries produce byte sequences that break our strict json decoder when unescaped mid-codepoint. our current error is unhelpful to customers.

oliver-eng: temporary workaround for customer: send args as a JSON object (not as a string) or base64-encode the inner payload. example payload that works:
```json
{\"tool\":\"create-note\",\"args\": {\"title\":\"Sync\",\"body\":\"Agenda: sync + emojis \ud83d\udc68\u200d\ud83d\udc69\u200d\ud83d\udc67\u200d\ud83d\udc66\"}}
```

oliver-eng: if they can't change client quickly, we can accept args as bytes (base64) server-side or normalize invalid sequences by escaping invalid runs before inner-unmarshal.

lisa-ml: opening ENG-1234 to track a fix: add utf8.ValidString() checks for inner decoding and fallback to unicode-escaped representation when invalid runs found. will add unit tests for:
- raw emoji
- ZWJ family chain
- truncated multibyte sequences
- args-as-string and args-as-object variations
